correctness.rationale: At equilibrium, the predator equation gives 1-e^{-beta x*}=s e^{s tau}/(alpha Y), and the prey equation gives y*=(rYx*/(s e^{s tau}))(1-x*/K). Hence y*>0 iff x*<K, yielding tau<(1/s)log(alpha Y(1-e^{-beta K})/s). At the printed parameters this equals 132.923341652608..., while the weaker condition that x* merely remain real lasts to 250.531764704813.... At tau=250 the printed formulas give x*=45.4889011125... and y*=-409.077854460..., so no positive coexistence equilibrium exists there. The analytic sign argument, not the floating-point checker, proves the claim.

value.rationale: The correction removes a large spurious interval of purported positive-equilibrium dynamics from the article's principal numerical example. The issue changes the interpretation of the bifurcation branch: the reported transcritical point 132.9233 is not merely an intermediate stability switch but the actual endpoint of positivity. This is mathematically and biologically substantive because coexistence requires positive densities; the correction aligns the example with the article's own general theorem rather than merely adjusting a rounded decimal.
